events.text:
⚡️🇺🇸 The yankees have announced their first Dark Eagle hypersonic missile battery is ready for deployment
Dark Eagle Long-Range Hypersonic Weapon (LRHW) battery, marking the introduction of a ground-based hypersonic strike capability into its operational arsenal. The missile reportedly travels at speeds exceeding Mach 5 and has an estimated range of approximately 2,775 km, allowing it to strike distant targets with conventional warheads.
The mobile battery consists of four launchers and is operated by the Army’s 1st Multi-Domain Task Force. Its deployment follows years of development delays, with additional batteries planned by 2028.
Per CBO estimates the system's costs are substantial:
Ground equipment per battery: approximately $40 million.
Each hypersonic missile: approximately $41–45 million.
Complete battery with eight missiles: approximately $370–400 million.
Note: These are just estimates, and their actual cost could be multifold higher.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: ‼️Drones attacked the industrial zone of Nevinnomyssk in Russia's Stavropol Krai overnight, with residents reporting more than 30 explosions. The city hosts Nevinnomyssky Azot, southern Russia's largest nitrogen fertilizer and chemical plant, which supplies raw materials to the Russian defense industry. ASTRA also reported a strike on the Nevinnomyssk thermal power plant. Regional authorities confirmed damage to industrial and energy infrastructure.

events.title: Telegram
events.text: ‼️Drones struck the Subkhankulovo oil pumping and dispatch station in the Tuymazinsky district of Russia's Bashkortostan overnight, sparking a fire. Operated by Transneft-Ural, the facility is a major hub in Russia's oil pipeline network, handling crude oil from Western Siberia and Tatarstan. Local authorities confirmed a fire at an industrial facility following a drone attack. The station was previously struck in July 2026.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defense Minister Israel Katz confirm the IDF struck and killed a senior Hamas government official in the central Gaza Strip overnight.
Khaled Abu Nada was responsible for Hamas's economy and education portfolio, the Israeli leaders say.
Netanyahu and Katz say the killing of Abu Nada is "part of a series of targeted killings carried out recently against members and senior officials of the organization."
"Around 80 Hamas terrorists have been killed over the past month, and our forces will continue to thwart and exact retribution against every terrorist in the terror organization," the joint statement adds.

events.text:
🇨🇳🇺🇸 US-China rivalry leaves Southeast Asia with fewer trade and foreign policy options – report
Growing competition between Washington and Beijing is narrowing Southeast Asian countries’ room for diplomatic maneuver, while leaving them increasingly exposed to trade and energy shocks, the South China Morning Post reports.
🌏 The US-Israeli war on Iran and disruption to energy supplies through the Strait of Hormuz hit the region particularly hard, driving up fuel and fertilizer costs
🌏 Vietnam suffered the biggest decline in power in the region, amid its heavy reliance on trade, which accounts for 190% of its GDP
🌏 Indonesia’s standing also fell, with analysts pointing to concerns over President Prabowo Subianto’s foreign policy and its departure from the country’s traditional non-alignment
🌏 The US lead over China in the Asia Power Index narrowed to its smallest margin since the index was launched in 2018
Analysts warn that smaller Southeast Asian states have less leverage as great-power rivalry intensifies.
